SAMIN-DURR:6:97#2/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:97#2/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:6:97#2/r1.claim: The apparent parse takes جعل as ‘created,’ with one object; لكم and لتهتدوا both attach to the verb.
SAMIN-DURR:6:97#2/r1.anchor: الظاهر أن " جعل " بمعنى خلق فتكون متعدية لواحد، و " لكم " متعلق ب " جعل " وكذا " لتهتدوا "

SAMIN-DURR:6:97#2/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:97#2/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:6:97#2/r2.claim: The repeated preposition is resolved by taking لتهتدوا as an appositional بدل of لكم, repeating its governor; لام كي makes the verb subjunctive after implicit أن for Basrans.
SAMIN-DURR:6:97#2/r2.anchor: فالجواب أن الثاني بدل من الأول بدل اشتمال بإعادة العامل، فإن " ليهتدوا " جار ومجرور، إذ اللام لام كي

SAMIN-DURR:6:97#2/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:97#2/r3.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:6:97#2/r3.claim: The sense is that God made the stars for guidance; al-Samin compares the construction with لبيوتهم in 43:33.
SAMIN-DURR:6:97#2/r3.anchor: والتقدير: جعل لكم النجوم لاهتدائكم، ونظيره في القرآن

SAMIN-DURR:6:97#2/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:97#2/r4.speaker: ابن عطية
SAMIN-DURR:6:97#2/r4.claim: Ibn ʿAtiyya allows جعل to mean ‘made,’ with its second object understood from لتهتدوا: the stars were made guidance for you.
SAMIN-DURR:6:97#2/r4.anchor: وقال ابن عطية: " وقد يمكن أن يكون بمعنى " صير " ويقدر المفعول الثاني من لتهتدوا

SAMIN-DURR:6:97#2/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:97#2/r5.speaker: الشيخ
SAMIN-DURR:6:97#2/r5.claim: The Shaykh calls Ibn ʿAtiyya’s parse weak because it requires omitting one of the two objects of ظن and its sisters.
SAMIN-DURR:6:97#2/r5.anchor: قال الشيخ: " وهو ضعيف لندور حذف أحد مفعولي ظن وأخواتها "

SAMIN-DURR:6:97#2/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:97#2/r6.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:6:97#2/r6.claim: Al-Samin defends Ibn ʿAtiyya: the prepositional complement functions as the second object, estimated as مستقرة أو كائنة لاهتدائكم; ‘stars as guidance’ clarifies the sense.
SAMIN-DURR:6:97#2/r6.anchor: قلت: لم يدع ابن عطية حذف المفعول الثاني حتى يجعله ضعيفا إنما قال: إنه من " لتهتدوا "

SAMIN-DURR:6:97#2/r7.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:97#2/r7.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:6:97#2/r7.claim: نجم was originally the verbal noun for a star’s emergence, then figuratively named the celestial body; النجوم can be noun or verbal noun.
SAMIN-DURR:6:97#2/r7.anchor: والنجم في الأصل مصدر يقال: نجم الكوكب ينجم نجما ونجوما فهو ناجم

SAMIN-DURR:6:97#2/r8.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:97#2/r8.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:6:97#2/r8.claim: نجم also describes plants sprouting and horns emerging; النجم is a plant without a stem, unlike a tree with a stem.
SAMIN-DURR:6:97#2/r8.anchor: والنجم من النبات ما لا ساق له، والشجر ما له ساق

SAMIN-DURR:6:97#2/r9.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:6:97#2/r9.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:6:97#2/r9.claim: التنجيم means separating or distributing; نجوم الكنانة is compared with scattered stars.

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p1070/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p1070/r1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p1070/r1.claim: Tafṣīl originates in separating things; it can mean broad explanation or the presentation of several distinct matters.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p1070/r1.anchor: التفصيل هو إما أن يكون التبيين والفصل هو الحجز بين الشيئين وهذا الأصل

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p1070/r2.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p1070/r2.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p1070/r2.claim: The passage moves across separate subjects—seeds, dawn, sun and moon, then stars—so its many different signs are appropriately called tafṣīl.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p1070/r2.anchor: إنتقل من الحب والنوى إلى الإصباح ثم الشمس والقمر ثم النجوم، مواضيع أخرى ثم ينتقل يذكر أموراً كثيرة

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p993/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p993/r1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p993/r1.claim: The conjunction wāw gives general coordination and may join one sentence to another; it does not itself express a causal relation.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p993/r1.anchor: الواو لمطلق الجمع، الجمع المطلق، قد يكون عطف جملة على جملة

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p993/r2.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p993/r2.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p993/r2.claim: Fa commonly marks cause and consequence, as in درس فنجح; when the first action leads to the next, fa is used rather than wāw.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p993/r2.anchor: الفاء تفيد السبب، هذا المشهور في معناها (درس فنجح)

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p85/.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p85/.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p85/.claim: After the sun and moon, attention turns to the stars as another sign serving the world's inhabitants.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p85/.anchor: After the sun and the moon, attention is directed to the stars

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p85/.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p85/.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p85/.claim: The stars' service to people testifies that the Creator deputed them for their role.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p85/.anchor: they bear witness that the creator has deputed them to this

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p86/.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p86/.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p86/.claim: Stars serve human travelers, so deifying them is foolish; their service to earth's people shows one God governs both heaven and earth and merits gratitude and worship.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p86/.anchor: they are serving the needs of those who live on the earth.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p86/.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p86/.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p86/.claim: Arab poets describe stars both as guides on night journeys and as markers of the hours of night, making them travel guides and clocks.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p86/.anchor: they serve both as clocks and as travel guides.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p86/.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p86/.speaker: the Arabs
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p86/.claim: Arabs worshipped some stars, including Sirius (shi‘rā), which appears in spring; they also treated some stars as auspicious and others as ill-omened.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p86/.anchor: the Arabs also worshipped certain stars. Thus, Sirius ( shi‘rā) has been referred to by the Qur’ ān.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p86/.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p86/.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p86/.claim: Here āyāt means signs and, because a sign proves what it signifies, also proofs and arguments.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p86/.anchor: Here it means “signs” and since every sign is a proof of the thing it is a sign of, it also means “proofs” and “arguments.”

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p86/.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p86/.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p86/.claim: The signs supply arguments chiefly for monotheism and also for the hereafter and prophethood; each sign has several aspects, while its referent is left for the curious audience to discern.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p86/.anchor: As monotheism is mentioned here and secondarily the hereafter and prophethood too are mentioned, it would here mean arguments and proofs about them.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p86/.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p86/.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p86/.claim: Against Quraysh's demand for a tangible miracle, the passage points to signs that satisfy intellect and heart; those who seek only the palpable remain blind even when miracles appear.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p86/.anchor: if they want to see miracles, then God has stated signs that satisfy the intellect and the heart.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p86/.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p86/.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p86/.claim: The phrase means people who want to know: sometimes a verb expresses the intention behind an action.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-anam-06:p86/.anchor: At times a verb is used to connote its intention. For this reason, the words

MUSNAD-AHMAD:12600/r1.author: Aḥmad b. Ḥanbal
MUSNAD-AHMAD:12600/r1.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
MUSNAD-AHMAD:12600/r1.claim: Anas reports the Prophet comparing scholars to stars that guide people through land and sea darkness; when stars vanish, guides may go astray, extending the verse's image of guidance by stars.
MUSNAD-AHMAD:12600/r1.anchor: أنه سمع أنس بن مالك يقول: قال النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم: " إن مثل العلماء في الأرض، كمثل النجوم في السماء

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p590/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p590/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p590/r3.claim: A star is called najm because it rises; Arabic says a plant has emerged when it sprouts.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p590/r3.anchor: النجم معروف سمي بذلك لطلوعه يقال نجم النبت إذا طلع

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p595/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p595/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p595/r1.claim: فصلنا means explaining and dividing the signs; people who know benefit from that detail, while others turn from the signs and their evidentiary force.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p595/r1.anchor: أي بينا وقسمنا وخص من يعلم لأنهم الذين ينتفعون بتفصيلها

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p596/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p596/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p596/r1.claim: The clear benefit of stars suits the ending يعلمون, since even basic understanding suffices; tracing creation from one soul through many states demands close thought, so يفقهون suits that verse.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v4p596/r1.anchor: لما كان الاهتداء بالنجوم واضحا ختمه بقوله: يعلمون

ALUSI-FULL:v7p233#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v7p233#2/r1.speaker: بعض المفسرين
ALUSI-FULL:v7p233#2/r1.claim: Some take “stars” to exclude the Sun and Moon, since guidance is the stated use and common usage calls the other heavenly bodies stars.
ALUSI-FULL:v7p233#2/r1.anchor: قيل : المراد بها ما عدا النيرين لأنها التي بها الاهتداء الآتي

ALUSI-FULL:v7p233#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v7p233#2/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v7p233#2/r2.claim: Alternatively, stars include the Sun and Moon, so this verse states their general benefit after the preceding verse gave their particular benefit.
ALUSI-FULL:v7p233#2/r2.anchor: وجوز أن يدخلا فيها فيكون هذا بيانا لفائدتهما العامة إثر بيان فائدتهما الخاصة

ALUSI-FULL:v7p233#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v7p233#2/r3.speaker: المنجمون
ALUSI-FULL:v7p233#2/r3.claim: Astrologers divide stars into fixed and wandering bodies; earlier authorities unanimously counted seven wanderers, while modern astrologers add Herschel as an eighth.
ALUSI-FULL:v7p233#2/r3.anchor: والمنجمون يقسمون النجوم إلى ثوبت وسيارات والسيارات سبع باجماع المتقدمين وثمان

ALUSI-FULL:v7p233#2/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v7p233#2/r4.speaker: عبد الرحمن الصوفي
ALUSI-FULL:v7p233#2/r4.claim: Al-Ṣūfī counts 1,025 observed fixed stars including the Coma constellation, or 1,022 when it is excluded; God alone knows their total.
ALUSI-FULL:v7p233#2/r4.anchor: والمرصود منها كما قال عبد الرحمن الصوفي : ألف وخمسة وعشرون بإدخال الضفيرة

ALUSI-FULL:v7p233#2/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v7p233#2/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v7p233#2/r5.claim: Astronomers classify fixed stars into six magnitudes, each with three grades, and devise other schemes; Alusi accepts only what entails no religiously objectionable consequence.
ALUSI-FULL:v7p233#2/r5.anchor: ورتبوا الثوابت على ست أقدار وسموها أقدارا متزائدة سدسا سدسا

ALUSI-FULL:v7p234/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v7p234/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v7p234/r1.claim: Li-tahtadū is an appositional substitute for the pronoun in “for you,” with the governing verb repeated as an apposition of inclusion.
ALUSI-FULL:v7p234/r1.anchor: بدل من ضمير ( لكم ) باعادة العامل بدل اشتمال كأنه قيل جعل النجوم

ALUSI-FULL:v7p234/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v7p234/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v7p234/r2.claim: The darknesses may mean night over land and sea, added by association, or confusing routes, called darknesses metaphorically.
ALUSI-FULL:v7p234/r2.anchor: أي في ظلمات الليل في البر والبحر واضافتها اليهما للملابسة أو في مشتبهات الطرق

ALUSI-FULL:v7p234/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v7p234/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v7p234/r3.claim: Navigation is singled out as the contextual benefit, though stars serve many further uses; like ordinary causes, they do not act independently.
ALUSI-FULL:v7p234/r3.anchor: وهذا إفراد لعض منافعها بالذكر حسبما يقتضيه المقام وإلا فهي أجدى من تفاريق العصا

ALUSI-FULL:v7p234/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v7p234/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v7p234/r4.claim: Learning astronomy, including constellations, lunar stations, and celestial positions, is permissible when used for a religious benefit.
ALUSI-FULL:v7p234/r4.anchor: ولا بأس في تعلم علم النجوم ومعرفة البروج والمنازل والأوضاع ونحو ذلك مما يتوصل به إلى مصلحة دينية

ALUSI-FULL:v7p234/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v7p234/r5.speaker: ابن حجر الهيتمي
ALUSI-FULL:v7p234/r5.claim: Ibn Hajar says forbidden astrology claims certain knowledge of future rain, snow, winds, prices, and similar events from the motions and configurations of stars; this knowledge belongs to God.
ALUSI-FULL:v7p234/r5.anchor: قال العلامة ابن حجر عليه الرحمة : والمنهي عنه من علم النجوم ما يدعيه أهلها من معرفة الحوادث الآتية

ALUSI-FULL:v7p234/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v7p234/r6.speaker: ابن حجر الهيتمي
ALUSI-FULL:v7p234/r6.claim: Ibn Hajar permits saying a conjunction is a customary divine sign that may fail, and permits observational astronomy for timekeeping and finding the qibla; the latter is a communal duty.
ALUSI-FULL:v7p234/r6.anchor: فأما من يقول : إن الاقتران أو الافتراق الذي هو كذا جعله الله تعالى علامة

ALUSI-FULL:v7p234/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v7p234/r7.speaker: زيد بن خالد الجهني والنبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
ALUSI-FULL:v7p234/r7.claim: After a rainy dawn prayer, the Prophet asks what God said: attributing rain to God expresses faith in Him and rejection of the stars, while attributing it to a lunar station reverses that.
ALUSI-FULL:v7p234/r7.anchor: وأما ما في حديث الصحيحين عن زيد بن خالد الجهني قال : صلى بنا رسول الله صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم

ALUSI-FULL:v7p234/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v7p234/r8.speaker: العلماء
ALUSI-FULL:v7p234/r8.claim: Scholars distinguish causation from signification: belief that a star causes rain is disbelief, while treating it as a fallible sign avoids disbelief but the wording remains disliked.
ALUSI-FULL:v7p234/r8.anchor: فقد قال العلماء : إنه محمول على ما إذا قال ذلك مريدا أن النوء هو المحدث

ALUSI-FULL:v7p234/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v7p234/r9.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
ALUSI-FULL:v7p234/r9.claim: A report from Ibn Abbas says acquiring knowledge of the stars is acquiring a branch of sorcery, with increased study increasing that share.
ALUSI-FULL:v7p234/r9.anchor: عن ابن عباس رضي الله تعالى عنهما قال : قال رسول الله صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم : من اقتبس علما من النجوم

ALUSI-FULL:v7p234/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v7p234/r10.speaker: ابن عباس
ALUSI-FULL:v7p234/r10.claim: Ibn Abbas advises Maimun ibn Mihran to fear God and avoid astrology because it leads to soothsaying.
ALUSI-FULL:v7p234/r10.anchor: عن ميمون بن مهران قال : قلت لابن عباس رضي الله تعالى عنهما أوصني قال أوصيك بتقوى الله

ALUSI-FULL:v7p234/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v7p234/r11.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
ALUSI-FULL:v7p234/r11.claim: A report from ʿAli says the Prophet forbade looking at the stars; similar reports are attributed to Abu Hurayra and ʿAisha.
ALUSI-FULL:v7p234/r11.anchor: عن علي كرم الله تعالى وجهه قال : نهاني رسول الله صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم عن النظر في النجوم

ALUSI-FULL:v7p234/r12.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v7p234/r12.speaker: أبو هريرة وعائشة
ALUSI-FULL:v7p234/r12.claim: Reports from Abu Hurayra and ʿAisha likewise transmit a prohibition on looking at the stars.
ALUSI-FULL:v7p234/r12.anchor: وعن أبي هريرة وعائشة رضي الله تعالى عنهما نحوه

ALUSI-FULL:v7p234/r13.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v7p234/r13.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
ALUSI-FULL:v7p234/r13.claim: A report from Ibn Abbas says one who studies Abjad letters and astrology will have no share with God on the Day of Resurrection.
ALUSI-FULL:v7p234/r13.anchor: عن ابن عباس رضي الله تعالى عنهما قال : قال رسول الله صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم : إن متعلم حروف أبي جادوراء في النجوم

ALUSI-FULL:v7p234/r14.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v7p234/r14.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
ALUSI-FULL:v7p234/r14.claim: A report from Ibn Umar urges learning from stars what guides travelers in land and sea darkness, then stopping there.
ALUSI-FULL:v7p234/r14.anchor: عن ابن عمر رضي الله تعالى عنهما قال : قال رسول الله صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم تعلموا من النجوم ما تهتدون به

ALUSI-FULL:v7p234/r15.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v7p234/r15.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v7p234/r15.claim: Alusi reads the warnings as blocking routes to prohibited astrology, especially soothsayers’ belief in stars’ independent effects and categorical predictions from their configurations.
ALUSI-FULL:v7p234/r15.anchor: ولعل ما تفيده من النهي عن التعلم من باب سد الذرائع لأن ذلك العلم ربما يجر إلى محظور شرعا

ALUSI-FULL:v7p234/r16.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v7p234/r16.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v7p234/r16.claim: No one except God can know everything placed in each star; partial knowledge cannot yield certainty and is like clinging to moonlight or sunlight.
ALUSI-FULL:v7p234/r16.anchor: على أن الوقوف على جميع ما أودع الله تعالى في كل كوكب مما يمتنع الغير علام الغيوب

ALUSI-FULL:v7p234/r17.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v7p234/r17.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v7p234/r17.claim: Some events regularly accompany a star’s rising, setting, or conjunction, as with the Pleiades and Canopus; reporting such experience as a customary, fallible sign is permissible under either account of causal efficacy.
ALUSI-FULL:v7p234/r17.anchor: نعم إن بعض الحوادث في عالم الكون والفساد قد جرت عادة الله تعالى بإحداثه في الغالب عند طلوع كوكب

ALUSI-FULL:v7p234/r18.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v7p234/r18.speaker: ابن عباس
ALUSI-FULL:v7p234/r18.claim: When a man hesitated to calculate the stars, ʿIkrima reportedly said Ibn Abbas wished he had learned a science people had neglected.
ALUSI-FULL:v7p234/r18.anchor: فقال عكرمة : سمعت ابن عباس رضي الله تعالى عنهما يقول : علم عجز الناس عنه

ALUSI-FULL:v7p234/r19.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v7p234/r19.speaker: عبد الله بن حفص
ALUSI-FULL:v7p234/r19.claim: A report from ʿAbd Allah ibn Hafs says Arabs had five traits—soothsaying, physiognomy, augury, astrology, and calculation—and Islam removed soothsaying while the rest persisted.
ALUSI-FULL:v7p234/r19.anchor: عن عبد الله بن حفص قال : خصت العرب بخصال بالكهانة والقيافة والعياقة والنجوم والحساب

ALUSI-FULL:v7p234/r20.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v7p234/r20.speaker: ابن عباس
ALUSI-FULL:v7p234/r20.claim: Al-Hasan ibn Salih says he heard Ibn Abbas call astrology a knowledge people had wasted; Alusi says this may mean the permissible empirical kind.
ALUSI-FULL:v7p234/r20.anchor: وقول الحسن بن صالح : سمعت عن ابن عباس رضي الله تعالى عنهما أنه قال في النجوم : ذلك علم

ALUSI-FULL:v7p234/r21.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v7p234/r21.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v7p234/r21.claim: Alusi concludes that astrology has no benefit and ignorance of it causes no harm: what God wills happens, and what He does not will does not.
ALUSI-FULL:v7p234/r21.anchor: وبعد هذا كله أقول : هو علم لا ينفع والجهل به لا يضر فما شاء الله تعالى كان

ALUSI-FULL:v7p234/r22.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v7p234/r22.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v7p234/r22.claim: “We have made the signs distinct” may mean the recited signs describing divine blessings, including the stars, or the created signs that disclose God’s attributes.
ALUSI-FULL:v7p234/r22.anchor: أي بينا الآيات المتلوة المذكورة لنعمه سبحانه التي هذه النعمة من جملتها أو الآيات التكوينية

ALUSI-FULL:v7p235/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v7p235/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v7p235/r1.claim: Those who know either act on the meaning of the revealed signs or contemplate created signs and understand reality; they are specified because they are the ones who benefit.
ALUSI-FULL:v7p235/r1.anchor: معني الآيات المذكورة فيعملون بموجبها أو يتفكرون في الآيات التكوينية فيعلمون حقيقة الحال

BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p170#2/r8.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p170#2/r8.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p170#2/r8.claim: God created the stars for people to find their way through the darkness of land and sea.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p170#2/r8.anchor: {وهو الذي جعل لكم النجوم} أي خلقها لكم، {لتهتدوا بها في ظلمات البر والبحر}

BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p170#2/r9.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p170#2/r9.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p170#2/r9.claim: A first benefit of stars is helping travelers at sea and in deserts find their destinations at night.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p170#2/r9.anchor: أحدها هذا: وهو أن [راكب البحر] (2) والسائر في القفار يهتدي بها في الليالي إلى مقاصده.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p170#2/r10.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p170#2/r10.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p170#2/r10.claim: Stars also adorn the sky, as stated in 67:5.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p170#2/r10.anchor: والثاني: أنها زينة للسماء كما قال: "ولقد زينا السماء الدنيا بمصابيح" (الملك، 5) .

BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p170#2/r11.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p170#2/r11.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p170#2/r11.claim: Stars also serve as missiles against devils, as stated in 67:5.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p170#2/r11.anchor: ومنها: رمي الشياطين، كما قال: "وجعلناها رجوما للشياطين"، (الملك، 5) .

BAYDAWI-FULL:6:97/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:6:97/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:6:97/r1.claim: God created the stars for human use.

BAYDAWI-FULL:6:97/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:6:97/r2.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:6:97/r2.claim: The darknesses may be the night on land and sea, associated with those settings, or confusing routes metaphorically called darknesses; guidance is one specified benefit after their benefits were summarized as being for people.
BAYDAWI-FULL:6:97/r2.anchor: في ظلمات الليل في البر والبحر، وإضافتها إليهما للملابسة أو في مشتبهات الطرق

BAYDAWI-FULL:6:97/r3.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:6:97/r3.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:6:97/r3.claim: God has explained the signs in detail, point by point.

BAYDAWI-FULL:6:97/r4.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:6:97/r4.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:6:97/r4.claim: Those who know are the ones who benefit from the detailed signs.

BIQAI-FULL:v2p680/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p680/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v2p680/r1.claim: God alone made all the stars, moving and fixed, for people to learn guidance from them, including finding the qibla and knowing prayer and fasting times for worldly and religious needs.
BIQAI-FULL:v2p680/r1.anchor: { لكم النجوم } أي كلها سائرها وثابتها وإن كان علمكم يقصر عنها كلها

BIQAI-FULL:v2p680/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p680/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v2p680/r2.claim: Land and water are naturally dark, compounded by night; the attribution of darkness to land and sea is by association, or by likening roads and other coverings to darkness.
BIQAI-FULL:v2p680/r2.anchor: الأرض والماء ليس لهما من نفسهما إلا الظلمة , وانضمت إلى ذلك ظلمة الليل

BIQAI-FULL:v2p680/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p680/r3.speaker: عمر بن الخطاب
BIQAI-FULL:v2p680/r3.claim: Umar advises learning enough astronomy for navigation and enough genealogy for kinship and lawful marriage knowledge, then stopping there.
BIQAI-FULL:v2p680/r3.anchor: عن عمر بن الخطاب رضي الله عنه قال : تعلموا من النجوم ما تهتدون في البر والبحر ثم انتهوا

BIQAI-FULL:v2p680/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p680/r4.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
BIQAI-FULL:v2p680/r4.claim: A report from Ali says the Prophet ordered complete ablution despite hardship, forbade taking charity, donkey-horse breeding, and sitting with astrologers.
BIQAI-FULL:v2p680/r4.anchor: عن علي رضي الله عنه قال : قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم : ( يا علي ! أسبغ الوضوء وإن شق عليك

BIQAI-FULL:v2p680/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p680/r5.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
BIQAI-FULL:v2p680/r5.claim: A report transmitted through Abu Dharr and Umar says the Prophet forbade asking about stars, interpreting the Qur'an by opinion, and abusing his Companions, calling that pure faith.
BIQAI-FULL:v2p680/r5.anchor: عن أبي ذر رضي الله عنه عن عمر رضي الله عنه قال : سمعت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يقول : ( لا تسألوا عن النجوم

BIQAI-FULL:v2p680/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p680/r6.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
BIQAI-FULL:v2p680/r6.claim: Abu Hurayra reports that the Prophet prohibited looking at the stars; the author says this report came through many routes.
BIQAI-FULL:v2p680/r6.anchor: عن أبي هريرة رضي الله عنه أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم نهى عن النظر في النجوم - رواه من طرق كثيرة

BIQAI-FULL:v2p680/r7.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p680/r7.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
BIQAI-FULL:v2p680/r7.claim: Aisha transmits the same prohibition against looking at the stars.
BIQAI-FULL:v2p680/r7.anchor: وعن عائشة رضي الله عنها مثله سواء

BIQAI-FULL:v2p680/r8.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p680/r8.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
BIQAI-FULL:v2p680/r8.claim: Ibn Masud reports the Prophet's instruction to refrain when the Companions, divine decree, or stars are mentioned; the report is transmitted through routes.
BIQAI-FULL:v2p680/r8.anchor: وعن ابن مسعود رضي الله عنه قال : قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم : ( إذا ذكر أصحابي فأمسكوا , وإذا ذكر القدر فأمسكوا

BIQAI-FULL:v2p681/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p681/r1.speaker: قتادة
BIQAI-FULL:v2p681/r1.claim: Qatada says stars are signs and were created for three purposes: adornment of heaven, guidance, and missiles against devils; using them otherwise is baseless speculation beyond one's knowledge.
BIQAI-FULL:v2p681/r1.anchor: وهذا الأثر الذي عن قتادة أخرجه عنه البخاري في صحيحه

BIQAI-FULL:v2p681/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p681/r2.speaker: صاحب كنز اليواقيت
BIQAI-FULL:v2p681/r2.claim: The cited book distinguishes beneficial from blameworthy knowledge: magic and talismans are blameworthy when used to harm, though knowing about them is not blameworthy in itself.
BIQAI-FULL:v2p681/r2.anchor: وقال صاحب كنز اليواقيت في استيعاب المواقيت في مقدمة الكتاب : واعلم أن العلم منه محمود

BIQAI-FULL:v2p681/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p681/r3.speaker: صاحب كنز اليواقيت
BIQAI-FULL:v2p681/r3.claim: The book cites an authentic report that the Prophet was bewitched and fell ill until Gabriel informed him and the spell was extracted from beneath a stone in a well.
BIQAI-FULL:v2p681/r3.anchor: وسحر النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم ومرض بسببه , حتى أخبره جبرئيل عليه السلام وأخرج السحر من تحت حجر في قعر بئر

BIQAI-FULL:v2p681/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p681/r4.speaker: صاحب كنز اليواقيت
BIQAI-FULL:v2p681/r4.claim: The book describes predictive astrology as inferring events from celestial causes, like a physician inferring illness from a pulse, but says the law censures it for weakening reliance on God, uncertainty, and lack of benefit.
BIQAI-FULL:v2p681/r4.anchor: كالقسم الثاني من علم النجوم الاحكامي المستدل به على الحوادث بالأسباب كاستدلال الطبيب بالنبض

BIQAI-FULL:v2p681/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p681/r5.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
BIQAI-FULL:v2p681/r5.claim: Ibn Abbas reports that the Prophet said acquiring astrological knowledge is acquiring a branch of magic, in proportion to how much one acquires.
BIQAI-FULL:v2p681/r5.anchor: عن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال : ( من اقتبس علما من النجوم اقتبس شعبة من السحر

BIQAI-FULL:v2p681/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p681/r6.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
BIQAI-FULL:v2p681/r6.claim: The author of the Book of Ornament cites a warning from the Prophet to avoid astrology because it leads to fortune-telling; no grading is given.
BIQAI-FULL:v2p681/r6.anchor: وروي عنه صلى الله عليه وسلم أنه قال : ( إياكم والنجوم ! فإنها تدعو إلى الكهانة

BIQAI-FULL:v2p681/r7.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p681/r7.speaker: صاحب كتاب الزينة
BIQAI-FULL:v2p681/r7.claim: The Book of Ornament's author says some sciences, including astronomy and script, originated with prophets and reached people through revelation; Idris was reportedly the first to teach astronomy.
BIQAI-FULL:v2p681/r7.anchor: قال : هذه الأشياء كلها لها أصل صحيح , فمنها ما كانت من علوم الأنبياء مثل النجوم والخط

BIQAI-FULL:v2p681/r8.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p681/r8.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v2p681/r8.claim: God has explained signs thoroughly, one after another, in an elevated pattern, so people able to know can infer the unseen from what they observe.
BIQAI-FULL:v2p681/r8.anchor: { قد فصلنا } أي بينا بيانا شافيا على ما لنا من العظمة { الآيات } واحدة في إثر واحدة

BIQAI-FULL:v2p681/r9.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v2p681/r9.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v2p681/r9.claim: After the earthly and heavenly dominion, the discourse turns to the human as a single comprehensive creation, demonstrating God's power and rebutting beliefs that lights and celestial bodies act by choice.
BIQAI-FULL:v2p681/r9.anchor: ولما ذكر سبحانه بعض هذا الملكوت الأرضي والسماوي , أتبعه - كما مضى في أول السورة - الخلق المفرد الجامع لجميع الملكوت

BURSEVI:v3p55#3/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p55#3/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p55#3/r4.claim: God arranged the stars in positions that vary north, south, east, and west.
BURSEVI:v3p55#3/r4.anchor: التي تختلف مواضعها من جهة الشمال والجنوب والصبا والدبور

BURSEVI:v3p55#3/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p55#3/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p55#3/r5.claim: The stars guide people on land and sea in the darkness of night; the darkness is associated with those settings because that is when guidance by stars is needed.
BURSEVI:v3p55#3/r5.anchor: في ظلمات الليل في البر والبحر وإضافتها إليهما للملابسة

BURSEVI:v3p55#3/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p55#3/r6.speaker: الحدادي
BURSEVI:v3p55#3/r6.claim: Al-Haddadi explains that travelers identify routes through deserts and seas at night by placing particular stars before, beside, or behind them.
BURSEVI:v3p55#3/r6.anchor: لتعرفوا بها الطرق من بلد إلى بلد في المفاوز

BURSEVI:v3p55#3/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p55#3/r7.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p55#3/r7.claim: Stars also adorn the sky and stone devils, among other benefits.
BURSEVI:v3p55#3/r7.anchor: وهي أنها زينة السماء ورمي الشياطين وغير ذلك

BURSEVI:v3p56/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p56/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p56/r1.claim: God has explained, detail by detail, the signs demonstrating His power; those who know benefit from them.
BURSEVI:v3p56/r1.anchor: أي بينا الآيات الدالة على قدرتنا فصلا فصلا

BURSEVI:v3p56#2/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p56#2/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p56#2/r1.claim: The signs in 6:97 concern the cosmic creation, while those in 6:98 detail human creation; cosmic signs are more apparent and call for knowing, whereas subtle human signs call for discerning understanding.
BURSEVI:v3p56#2/r1.anchor: وإنما ذكر مع ذكر النجوم يعلمون ومع ذكر تخليق بني آدم يفقهون لأن ذلك إشارة إلى آيات الآفاق

BURSEVI:v3p56#2/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p56#2/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p56#2/r4.claim: Cosmic and human signs disclose God's wondrous work and call polytheists to tawhid, sincere believers to direct witnessing, and sinners to obedience and repentance of tongue and heart.
BURSEVI:v3p56#2/r4.anchor: ثم هذه الآيات الآفاقية والأنفسية تفصح عن صنع الله البديع وتدعو أهل الشرك إلى التوحيد

BURSEVI:v3p56#2/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p56#2/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p56#2/r5.claim: Great blessings call for gratitude and recognition of their due; each person's path to realization follows the gift received, whether unification of divine acts, attributes, or essence.
BURSEVI:v3p56#2/r5.anchor: فإن الامتنان بذكر النعم الجليلة يستدعي شكرا لها ومعرفة لحقها ولكل قوم وفريق سلوك إلى طريق التحقيق

BURSEVI:v3p56#2/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p56#2/r6.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p56#2/r6.claim: A rational person must seek the Real; the ordered cosmic and human worlds are means to reach what is manifest through its manifestations, while heedlessness is the true veil.
BURSEVI:v3p56#2/r6.anchor: فعلى العاقل أن يجتهد في طلب الحق فإن المقصود من ترتيب مقدمات العوالم آفاقية كانت أو أنفسية

BURSEVI:v3p56#2/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p56#2/r7.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p56#2/r7.claim: An anecdote tells how Shahin ibn Shuja al-Kirmani, a king who had gone hunting, met a youth riding a lion among wild beasts; the youth rebuked his heedlessness and worldliness, saying God gave the world to help people serve Him.
BURSEVI:v3p56#2/r7.anchor: وحكي أن الشيخ أبا الفوارس شاهين بن شجاع الكرماني رحمه الله خرج للصيد وهو ملك كرمان

BURSEVI:v3p56#2/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p56#2/r8.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p56#2/r8.claim: In the anecdote, an old woman brought the youth water, and Shahin found it exceptionally sweet; the youth said the world had been assigned to serve him, supplying what he needed, and quoted God telling the world to serve whoever serves Him and enslave whoever serves it; Shahin repented.
BURSEVI:v3p56#2/r8.anchor: هذه الدنيا وكلها الله إلى خدمتي فما احتجت إلى شيء إلا أحضرته إلي حين يخطر ببالي

DURR-FULL:v3p328/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p328/r1.speaker: مسلم بن يسار
DURR-FULL:v3p328/r1.claim: Muslim ibn Yasār reports a Prophetic prayer asking God, as splitter of dawn and maker of night's repose, to settle debts, relieve poverty, and preserve hearing, sight, and strength for His cause.
DURR-FULL:v3p328/r1.anchor: عن مسلم بن يسار قال: كان دعاء النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم اللهم فالق الأصباح وجاعل الليل سكنا والشمس والقمر حسبانا

DURR-FULL:v3p328/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p328/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v3p328/r2.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās explains the darknesses of land and sea as darkness and deviation from the road in which a traveler may become lost.
DURR-FULL:v3p328/r2.anchor: عن ابن عباس في قوله {وهو الذي جعل لكم النجوم لتهتدوا بها في ظلمات البر والبحر} قال: يضل الرجل

DURR-FULL:v3p328/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p328/r3.speaker: عمر بن الخطاب
DURR-FULL:v3p328/r3.claim: ʿUmar permits learning stars for land and sea navigation, then says to stop; stars adorn heaven, repel devils, and guide travelers, while genealogy and rules of marriage are also useful knowledge.
DURR-FULL:v3p328/r3.anchor: عن عمر بن الخطاب قال: تعلموا من النجوم ما تهتدون به في بركم وبحركم ثم امسكوا

DURR-FULL:v3p328/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p328/r4.speaker: قتادة
DURR-FULL:v3p328/r4.claim: Qatāda says stars have three purposes: adornment of heaven, navigation, and missiles against devils; astrology and predictions based on birth or travel under a star are ignorant guesses without knowledge.
DURR-FULL:v3p328/r4.anchor: عن قتادة قال: إن الله إنما جعل هذه النجوم لثلاث خصال جعلها زينة للسماء وجعلها يهتدى بها وجعلها رجوما للشياطين

DURR-FULL:v3p328/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p328/r5.speaker: ابن عمر
DURR-FULL:v3p328/r5.claim: Ibn ʿUmar reports the Prophet's instruction to learn from stars for navigation on land and sea, then stop.
DURR-FULL:v3p328/r5.anchor: عن ابن عمر قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم تعلموا من النجوم ما تهتدون به في ظلمات البر والبحر ثم انتهوا

DURR-FULL:v3p328/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p328/r6.speaker: مجاهد
DURR-FULL:v3p328/r6.claim: Mujāhid permits learning from stars for navigation and learning the lunar mansions.
DURR-FULL:v3p328/r6.anchor: عن مجاهد قال: لا بأس أن يتعلم الرجل من النجوم ما يهتدي به في البر والبحر ويتعلم منازل القمر

DURR-FULL:v3p328/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p328/r7.speaker: حميد الشامي
DURR-FULL:v3p328/r7.claim: Ḥumayd al-Shāmī says the stars are among the knowledge given to Adam.
DURR-FULL:v3p328/r7.anchor: عن حميد الشامي قال: النجوم هي علم آدم عليه السلام

IBNABIHATIM:v4p1355#2/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1355#2/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1355#2/r1.claim: The stars guide a person who has lost his way in darkness and strayed from the road.
IBNABIHATIM:v4p1355#2/r1.anchor: عن ابن عباس : قوله : وهو الذين جعل لكم النجوم لتهتدوا بها في ظلمات البرو والبحر ، قال : يضل الرجل ، وهو في الظلمة والجور عن الطريق

IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p392#2/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p392#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p392#2/r1.claim: The verse is linked to the preceding mention of making night a repose; it recalls divine oneness, the stars' wondrous creation, and their benefit as guides on land and sea.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p392#2/r1.anchor: عطف على جملة : { وجاعل الليل سكنا } ( الأنعام : 96 ) ، وهذا تذكير بوحدانية الله

IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p392#2/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p392#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p392#2/r2.claim: The mapping of stellar motions and risings and settings was among humanity's oldest sciences, appearing among Chaldeans and ancient Egyptians and guiding the development of astronomy.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p392#2/r2.anchor: وقد كان ضبط حركات النجوم ومطالعها ومغاربها من أقدم العلوم البشرية

IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p392#2/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p392#2/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p392#2/r3.claim: The main aim is to prove God's unique divinity; defining both subject and predicate makes the clause restrictive, though the audience already acknowledged God's creation of stars and their usefulness.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p392#2/r3.anchor: فلذلك صيغ بصيغة القصر بطريق تعريف المسند والمسند إليه

IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p392#2/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p392#2/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p392#2/r4.claim: Stars are the celestial bodies that shine in the night sky and appear small to the eye; the moon is not a star.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p392#2/r4.anchor: والنجوم جمع نجم ، وهو الكوكب ، أي الجسم الكروي المضيء في الأفق ليلا

IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p392#2/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p392#2/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p392#2/r5.claim: Here ja'ala means created and takes one object; lakum attaches to it, addresses all humanity, and its lām expresses purpose.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p392#2/r5.anchor: و { جعل } هنا بمعنى خلق ، فيتعدى إلى مفعول واحد و { لكم } . متعلق

IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p393/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p393/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p393/r1.claim: The guidance clause is a second purpose of creation; the first lām expresses benefaction, while the second gives the wisdom and benefit, and guidance is nearly an explicative substitute with its governing verb repeated.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p393/r1.anchor: وقوله : { لتهتدوا بها } علة ثانية ل { جعل } فاللام للعلة أيضا

IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p393/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p393/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p393/r2.claim: Darknesses means intense darkness; Arabic commonly uses the plural rather than the singular for this sense, as in the earlier verse about people left in darknesses.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p393/r2.anchor: والمراد بالظلمات : الظلمة الشديدة ، فصيغة الجمع مستعملة في القوة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p393/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p393/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p393/r3.claim: The annexation can mean darknesses occurring in land and sea; those rejecting an in-meaning take it as a lām-relation of slight association, like the expression planet of the awkward woman.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p393/r3.anchor: وإضافة ظلمات } إلى { البر والبحر } على معنى ( في ) لأن الظلمات

IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p393/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p393/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p393/r4.claim: The apparent account in al-Miftah treats slight-association annexation as a similarity-based metaphor, like the earth swallowing its water in 11:44.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p393/r4.anchor: فهو استعارة على ما هو ظاهر كلام ( المفتاح ) في مبحث البلاغة والفصاحة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p393/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p393/r5.speaker: التفتزاني
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p393/r5.claim: Al-Taftazani calls slight-association annexation a figurative attribution, since literal lām-annexation expresses complete relation or ownership.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p393/r5.anchor: إذ قال في ( كوكب الخرقاء ) ( حقيقة الإضافة اللامية الاختصاص الكامل

IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p393/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p393/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p393/r6.claim: Ibn Ashur suggests al-Taftazani may distinguish the figures by how closely the slight association approaches ownership; the phrase itself suggests figurative attribution.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p393/r6.anchor: ولعل التفتزاني يرى الاختلاف في المجاز باختلاف قرب الإضافة لأدنى ملابسة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p394/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p394/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p394/r1.claim: The independent sentence records and delivers the signs to remove excuses from unbelievers; its lām makes the detailed signs serve those who know.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p394/r1.anchor: وجملة : { قد فصلنا الآيات } مستأنفة للتسجيل والتبليغ وقطع معذرة من لم يؤمنوا

IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p394/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p394/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p394/r2.claim: The detailing of signs was discussed earlier in the sura at 6:55.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p394/r2.anchor: وتفصيل الآيات تقدم عند قوله تعالى : { وكذلك نفصل الآيات في هذه السورة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p394/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p394/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p394/r3.claim: The definite article is comprehensive, covering the sign of creating stars and all other signs.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p394/r3.anchor: والتعريف في الآيات } للاستغراق فيشمل آية خلق النجوم وغيرها

IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p394/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p394/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p394/r4.claim: Knowledge in Arabic is apprehending things as they are; two cited poets contrast the knowledgeable person with the ignorant.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p394/r4.anchor: والعلم في كلام العرب إدراك الأشياء على ما هي عليه قال السموأل أو عبد الملك الحارثي

IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p394/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p394/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p394/r5.claim: Those who know are people who benefit from the signs and believe in God alone, as stated at 6:99.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v7p394/r5.anchor: وهم الذين آمنوا بالله وحده ، كما قال تعالى : { إن في ذلكم لآيات لقوم يؤمنون

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p326#2/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p326#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p326#2/r1.claim: The address includes believers and unbelievers: proof against the latter and a lesson available to the former.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p326#2/r1.anchor: هذه المخاطبة تعم المؤمنين والكافرين، فالحجة بها على الكافرين قائمة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p326#2/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p326#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p326#2/r2.claim: Jaʿala means created because it takes one object; it may mean appointed with guidance as an implied second object after li-tahtadū.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p326#2/r2.anchor: وجعل هنا بمعنى خلق لدخولها على مفعول واحد

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p326#2/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p326#2/r3.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p326#2/r3.claim: Darkness can mean actual night, since stars appear only at night, or hardships in places where people navigate by the sun.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p326#2/r3.anchor: وفي ظلمات هي هاهنا على حقيقتها في ظلمة الليل

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p326#2/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p326#2/r4.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p326#2/r4.claim: The Qurʾān names three star uses: adornment, missiles against devils, and guidance.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p326#2/r4.anchor: وذكر الله تعالى النجوم في ثلاث منافع وهي قوله: ولقد زينا السماء الدنيا

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p326#2/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p326#2/r5.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p326#2/r5.claim: Other astrological claims are false fabrications against God and unbelief.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p326#2/r5.anchor: فالواجب أن يعتقد أن ما عدا هذه الوجوه من قول أهل التأثير باطل

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p326#2/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p326#2/r6.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p326#2/r6.claim: Faṣṣalnā means clarified and divided, āyāt means proofs; people who know recognize the sign while others ignore it.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p326#2/r6.anchor: وفصلنا معناه بينا وقسمنا والآيات الدلائل

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p91/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p91/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p91/r1.anchor: جعل بمعنى خلق وإنما امتن عليهم بالنجوم

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p91/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p91/r2.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p91/r2.claim: God's favor in creating stars is that land travelers and sailors use them at night to find their destinations.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p91/r2.anchor: لأن سالكي القفاء وراكبي البحار إنما يهتدون في الليل لمقاصدهم بها

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p305/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p305/r1.speaker: بعض السلف
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p305/r1.claim: Some early authorities say the stars have three divinely intended uses: adornment of heaven, missiles against devils, and navigation on land and sea; believing otherwise is error and a lie about God.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p305/r1.anchor: قال بعض السلف: من اعتقد في هذه النجوم غير ثلاث

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p305/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p305/r2.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p305/r2.claim: God has made the signs clear and explained them.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p305/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p305/r3.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p305/r3.claim: Those who know are people who reason, recognize the truth, and avoid falsehood.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p305/r3.anchor: أي: يعقلون ويعرفون الحق ويجتنبون (2) الباطل.

JISHUMI:v3p2333#2/r4.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v3p2333#2/r4.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v3p2333#2/r4.claim: Jaʿl can mean creation, as in making the stars and making darkness and light.
JISHUMI:v3p2333#2/r4.anchor: الجعل والفعل من النظائر، والجعل ينصرف على أربعة أوجه

JISHUMI:v3p2333#2/r5.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v3p2333#2/r5.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v3p2333#2/r5.claim: Jaʿl has four senses: create, transform one thing into another, make or cause something to become so, and judge or deem.
JISHUMI:v3p2333#2/r5.anchor: الثاني: بمعنى القلب كقولهم: جعل الطين خزفا

JISHUMI:v3p2333#2/r6.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v3p2333#2/r6.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v3p2333#2/r6.claim: Nujūm derives from emergence; teeth and horns are said to emerge, and it can name stemless plants or be a proper name for the Pleiades.
JISHUMI:v3p2333#2/r6.anchor: والنجوم: جمع نجم، وهو مأخوذ من نجم أي: طلع، يقال: نجم السن

JISHUMI:v3p2333#2/r7.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v3p2333#2/r7.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v3p2333#2/r7.claim: Ihtidāʾ is following the path of guidance: God points someone toward right conduct and the person recognizes it.
JISHUMI:v3p2333#2/r7.anchor: والاهتداء: سلوك طريق الهدى، يقال: هداه فاهتدى؛ أي: دله على الرشد

JISHUMI:v3p2333#2/r8.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v3p2333#2/r8.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v3p2333#2/r8.claim: Tafṣīl is explaining things through evidence, one part at a time.
JISHUMI:v3p2333#2/r8.anchor: والتفصيل: تبيين الأشياء بالدلائل فصلا فصلا

JISHUMI:v3p2337/r1.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v3p2337/r1.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v3p2337/r1.claim: The stars display God's great blessings, power, and oneness, providing benefits for religion and worldly life.
JISHUMI:v3p2337/r1.anchor: تدل الآية على عظيم نعمه في النجوم، وعلى قدرته وتوحيده، وأنه يجمع منافع الدين والدنيا

MUQATIL:6:95-99/r11.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:6:95-99/r11.speaker: author
MUQATIL:6:95-99/r11.claim: God made the stars lights by which travelers recognize their route at night on land and sea.
MUQATIL:6:95-99/r11.anchor: { وهو الذي جعل لكم النجوم } نورا، { لتهتدوا بها } بالكواكب ليلا، يقول: لتعرفوا الطريق إذا سرتم،

MUQATIL:6:95-99/r12.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:6:95-99/r12.speaker: author
MUQATIL:6:95-99/r12.claim: The signs are explained for people who know that God is one and has no partner.
MUQATIL:6:95-99/r12.anchor: { في ظلمات البر والبحر قد فصلنا الآيات لقوم يعلمون } [آية: 97] بأن الله واحد لا شريك له،

NASAFI-FULL:v1p336#3/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p336#3/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p336#3/r1.claim: God created the stars for people to use as guides.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p336#3/r1.anchor: ﴿ وهو الذي جعل لكم النجوم ﴾ خلقها ﴿ لتهتدوا بها فى ظلمات البر والبحر ﴾ أى فى ظلمات الليل

NASAFI-FULL:v1p336#3/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p336#3/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p336#3/r2.claim: The darkness is night over the land and sea; alternatively, confusing routes are likened to darkness.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p336#3/r2.anchor: ﴿ لتهتدوا بها في ظلمات البر والبحر ﴾ أى فى ظلمات الليل

NASAFI-FULL:v1p336#3/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p336#3/r3.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p336#3/r3.claim: The signs explained for people who know are signs pointing to God's oneness.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p336#3/r3.anchor: قد بينا الآيات الدالة على التوحيد لقوم يعلمون

QURTUBI-FULL:6:97/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:6:97/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:6:97/r1.claim: Stars demonstrate God's complete power and have many benefits; this verse mentions guidance on land and sea among benefits religious knowledge recommends.
QURTUBI-FULL:6:97/r1.anchor: بين كمال قدرته، وفي النجوم منافع جمة

QURTUBI-FULL:6:97/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:6:97/r2.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:6:97/r2.claim: The Qur'an also says stars guard against every rebellious devil.

QURTUBI-FULL:6:97/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:6:97/r3.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:6:97/r3.claim: Another verse says the stars were made as missiles for devils.

QURTUBI-FULL:6:97/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:6:97/r5.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:6:97/r5.claim: God explained the signs in detail to make reflection more effective; knowledgeable people are singled out because they benefit.
QURTUBI-FULL:6:97/r5.anchor: { قد فصلنا الآيات } أي بيناها مفصلة لتكون أبلغ في الاعتبار

QASHANI:6:97-98/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:6:97-98/r1.speaker: author
QASHANI:6:97-98/r1.claim: The stars are the senses: they guide through the body’s land to livelihood and through the heart’s sea to acquired knowledge.
QASHANI:6:97-98/r1.anchor: بر الأجساد إلى مصالح المعاش وبحر القلوب باكتساب العلوم بها

QASHANI:6:97-98/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:6:97-98/r2.speaker: author
QASHANI:6:97-98/r2.claim: The signs detailed for knowers are the spirit, the heart, and the senses.
QASHANI:6:97-98/r2.anchor: أي: الروح والقلب والحواس { لقوم يعلمون } ذلك

RAZI-FULL:v13p82/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v13p82/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v13p82/r1.claim: The stars are a third class of signs of divine power, mercy, and wisdom, created for people’s benefit.
RAZI-FULL:v13p82/r1.anchor: هذا هو النوع الثالث من الدلائل الدالة على كمال القدرة والرحمة والحكمة

RAZI-FULL:v13p82/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v13p82/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v13p82/r2.claim: Stars guide travelers on routes through dark land and sea when neither sun nor moon is visible.
RAZI-FULL:v13p82/r2.anchor: خلقها لتهتدي الخلق بها إلى الطرق والمسالك في ظلمات البر والبحر حيث لا يرون شمسا ولا قمرا

RAZI-FULL:v13p82/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v13p82/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v13p82/r3.claim: People use the sun’s movement to identify prayer times and daytime qibla, and the stars at night to identify the qibla.
RAZI-FULL:v13p82/r3.anchor: الناس يستدلون بأحوال حركة الشمس على معرفة أوقات الصلاة

RAZI-FULL:v13p82/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v13p82/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v13p82/r4.claim: Elsewhere the Qurʾan says the stars adorn the heaven, citing 25:61, 37:6, and 85:1.

RAZI-FULL:v13p82/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v13p82/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v13p82/r5.claim: The stars also serve as missiles against devils.
RAZI-FULL:v13p82/r5.anchor: أنه تعالى ذكر في منافعها كونها رجوما للشياطين

RAZI-FULL:v13p82/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v13p82/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v13p82/r6.claim: Razi offers a figurative reading: stars guide against the darkness of denying God’s voluntary agency and anthropomorphically assigning Him bodily location.

RAZI-FULL:v13p82/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v13p82/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v13p82/r7.claim: Their varied motion, position, brightness, and size show that identical bodies receive their properties by specification of a voluntary agent.
RAZI-FULL:v13p82/r7.anchor: نشاهد هذه الكواكب مختلفة في صفات كثيرة

RAZI-FULL:v13p82/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v13p82/r8.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v13p82/r8.claim: Stars are finite, composed, changing bodies; if these traits disqualify them as gods, God must be transcendent beyond body, parts, limits, place, and direction.
RAZI-FULL:v13p82/r8.anchor: وإن كانت عيوبا في الإلهية وجب تنزيه الإله عنها بأسرها

RAZI-FULL:v13p82/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v13p82/r9.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v13p82/r9.claim: Although this moves from the literal wording to metaphor, Razi says the interpretation closely suits the majesty of the Qurʾan.
RAZI-FULL:v13p82/r9.anchor: وهذا وإن كان عدولا عن حقيقة اللفظ إلى مجازه إلا أنه قريب مناسب لعظمة كتاب الله تعالى

RAZI-FULL:v13p85#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v13p85#2/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v13p85#2/r2.claim: The stars verse ends with yaʿlamun and the human-creation verse with yafqahun; creating humans from one source and varying their states is subtler workmanship, so fiqh signals greater insight and intelligence.
RAZI-FULL:v13p85#2/r2.anchor: أنه تعالى ختم الآية السابقة ، وهي الآية التي استدل فيها بأحوال النجوم

STUDYQURAN:6:96/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:6:96/r1.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:6:96/r1.claim: The cleaving and duality of verses 96–97 continue themes introduced in verse 95.
STUDYQURAN:6:96/r1.anchor: The themes of “cleaving” and duality presented in v. 95 continue in these two verses.

STUDYQURAN:6:96/r5.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:6:96/r5.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:6:96/r5.claim: Stars provide spatial orientation when the sun and moon are absent.
STUDYQURAN:6:96/r5.anchor: v. 97 mentions the stars as a means of spatial orientation by which people can be guided

STUDYQURAN:6:96/r6.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:6:96/r6.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:6:96/r6.claim: The darkness can mean literal night or, symbolically, moral and intellectual error and misguidance.
STUDYQURAN:6:96/r6.anchor: referring to either the physical darkness of the night or, symbolically, the moral and intellectual darkness of error and misguidance

STUDYQURAN:6:96/r7.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:6:96/r7.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:6:96/r7.claim: On the symbolic reading, sun, moon, and stars represent distinct degrees of moral guidance and spiritual illumination.
STUDYQURAN:6:96/r7.anchor: the sun, moon, and stars can represent different levels of moral guidance and spiritual illumination

STUDYQURAN:6:96/r8.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:6:96/r8.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:6:96/r8.claim: The Quran groups these celestial bodies in Abraham’s argument and Joseph’s dream.
STUDYQURAN:6:96/r8.anchor: The Quran frequently invokes the sun, moon, and stars together: for example, in Abraham’s argument in vv. 76–78 and in Joseph’s dream

STUDYQURAN:6:96/r9.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:6:96/r9.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:6:96/r9.claim: The sun, moon, and stars are made subject to God’s command and are described as prostrating to Him.
STUDYQURAN:6:96/r9.anchor: these three kinds of celestial bodies are also described as made subservient by His Command

STUDYQURAN:6:96/r10.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:6:96/r10.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:6:96/r10.claim: Other verses also describe the celestial bodies as prostrating to God.
STUDYQURAN:6:96/r10.anchor: as prostrating to Him (22:18); see also 55:5–6

STUDYQURAN:6:96/r11.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:6:96/r11.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:6:96/r11.claim: Expounding the signs means explaining them in detail.
STUDYQURAN:6:96/r11.anchor: that is, He explained them in detail, for a people who know

STUDYQURAN:6:96/r12.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:6:96/r12.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:6:96/r12.claim: Those who know possess intellect, reflect correctly, and reason from sensory experience and the seen toward the intellectual and unseen.
STUDYQURAN:6:96/r12.anchor: who reason from sensory realities to intellectual ones and from the seen to the unseen

TAB-FULL:v9p431#2/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v9p431#2/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v9p431#2/r1.claim: God made the stars guides for people lost or disoriented on land and sea at night, enabling them to find the route and escape their confusion.
TAB-FULL:v9p431#2/r1.anchor: عن ابن عباس، قوله: {وهو الذي جعل لكم النجوم لتهتدوا بها في ظلمات البر والبحر} [الأنعام: 97] قال: «يضل الرجل

TAB-FULL:v9p431#2/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v9p431#2/r2.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v9p431#2/r2.claim: The darknesses include night, error and misguidance, and the darkness of land or water.
TAB-FULL:v9p431#2/r2.anchor: وعنى بالظلمات: ظلمة الليل، وظلمة الخطأ والضلال، وظلمة الأرض أو الماء

TAB-FULL:v9p431#2/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v9p431#2/r3.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v9p431#2/r3.claim: The guidance echoes the statement that people are guided by landmarks and the star in 16:16.
TAB-FULL:v9p431#2/r3.anchor: كما قال جل ثناؤه: {وعلامات وبالنجم هم يهتدون} [النحل: 16]

TAB-FULL:v9p431#2/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v9p431#2/r4.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v9p431#2/r4.claim: God distinguishes and explains proofs so knowledgeable people can reflect, understand, leave ignorance and error, and stop persisting in knowingly obstinate wrongdoing.

TAB-FULL:v9p431#2/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v9p431#2/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v9p431#2/r5.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās describes a person lost in darkness and straying from the road.
TAB-FULL:v9p431#2/r5.anchor: عن ابن عباس، قوله: {وهو الذي جعل لكم النجوم لتهتدوا بها في ظلمات البر والبحر} [الأنعام: 97] قال: «يضل الرجل وهو في الظلمة والجور عن الطريق»

SULAMI:v1p209#6/r1.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p209#6/r1.speaker: أبو علي الجوزجاني
SULAMI:v1p209#6/r1.claim: God made night a mount for seeking nearness and a guide to the paths of divine approval; the stars guide people along the way to Paradise.
SULAMI:v1p209#6/r1.anchor: قال أبو علي الجوزجاني : جعل الله تعالى الليل مطية ودليلا ، فالمطية يركبها في طلب الزلف

TABATABAI:6:97-98/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:6:97-98/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:6:97-98/r1.claim: God arranged the stars so people can find their way across land and sea; the verse’s meaning is straightforward.
TABATABAI:6:97-98/r1.anchor: قوله تعالى { وهو الذي جعل لكم النجوم لتهتدوا بها } إلى آخر الآية

TABATABAI:6:97-98/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:6:97-98/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:6:97-98/r2.claim: The detailing of the signs may refer either to their specification through creation or to their exposition in words.
TABATABAI:6:97-98/r2.anchor: والمراد بتفصيل الآيات إما تفصيلها بحسب الجعل التكويني أو تفصيلها بحسب البيان اللفظي

TABATABAI:6:97-98/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:6:97-98/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:6:97-98/r3.claim: Stars’ practical benefit to human life does not conflict with each celestial body also being independently intended and created by divine will; the aspects differ and the world’s parts are interconnected.
TABATABAI:6:97-98/r3.anchor: ولا تنافي بين إرادة مصالح الإنسان في حياته وعيشته في هذه النشأة مما يتراءى لظاهر الحس من حركات هذه الاجرام العظيمة العلوية

TABATABAI:6:99-100/r12.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:6:99-100/r12.speaker: author
TABATABAI:6:99-100/r12.claim: The verse pairs each kind of sign with a capacity: stars address people who know, human creation those who understand deeply, and the growing system those who believe.
TABATABAI:6:99-100/r12.anchor: وقد عد النجوم آية خاصة بقوم يعلمون، وإنشاء النفوس الإنسانية آية خاصة بقوم يفقهون، وتدبير نظام الإنبات آية لقوم يؤمنون

TABRISI:6:97-98/r8.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:6:97-98/r8.speaker: author
TABRISI:6:97-98/r8.claim: God created stars for human benefit and guidance in travel, navigation, finding the qibla, reckoning night hours, and following land and sea routes by their light, rising, and positions.
TABRISI:6:97-98/r8.anchor: لأن من النجوم ما يكون بين يدي الإنسان ومنها ما يكون خلفه ومنها ما يكون عن يمينه

TABRISI:6:97-98/r9.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:6:97-98/r9.speaker: البلخي
TABRISI:6:97-98/r9.claim: The guidance purpose does not exclude other great purposes; varied star sizes, courses, and relations, and the sun and moon's benefits to life, show this.

TABRISI:6:97-98/r10.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:6:97-98/r10.speaker: علي بن إبراهيم بن هاشم
TABRISI:6:97-98/r10.claim: In the Tafsīr of ʿAlī ibn Ibrāhīm ibn Hāshim, the stars signify the family of Muhammad.
TABRISI:6:97-98/r10.anchor: وفي تفسير علي بن إبراهيم بن هاشم أن النجوم آل محمد ع

TABRISI:6:97-98/r11.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:6:97-98/r11.speaker: author
TABRISI:6:97-98/r11.claim: The signs have been made clear as proofs and evidences for people who reflect and thereby know.
TABRISI:6:97-98/r11.anchor: أي بينا الحجج والبينات: { لقوم يعلمون

THALABI:v4p172/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v4p172/r2.speaker: author
THALABI:v4p172/r2.claim: God created the stars to guide people through the darknesses of land and sea.
THALABI:v4p172/r2.anchor: وهو الذي جعل لكم النجوم أي خلقها لتهتدوا بها في ظلمات البر والبحر

THALABI:v4p172/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v4p172/r3.speaker: author
THALABI:v4p172/r3.claim: God has made the signs clear for people who know.
THALABI:v4p172/r3.anchor: قد فصلنا الآيات لقوم يعلمون وهو الذي أنشأكم خلقكم

ELMALILI:6:97/r1.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:6:97/r1.speaker: author
ELMALILI:6:97/r1.claim: His rendering says God made the stars a means for finding the way on land and sea and elaborated the signs for people of knowledge.
ELMALILI:6:97/r1.anchor: karada ve denizde yolu doğrultmanız için size yıldızları sebep kılmıştır. Hakikat ilim ehli olanlar için âyetleri tafsil eyledik

ELMALILI:6:97/r2.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:6:97/r2.speaker: author
ELMALILI:6:97/r2.claim: God made the stars for human benefit, not humans for the stars; they are lamps of guidance and signs of mercy, not ruling or managing deities.
ELMALILI:6:97/r2.anchor: sizi nücum için değil, nücûmu sizin için, sizin intifâ‘ınız

ELMALILI:6:97/r3.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:6:97/r3.speaker: author
ELMALILI:6:97/r3.claim: Their indications help people orient their destination, directions, qibla, and both material and spiritual paths through land and sea.
ELMALILI:6:97/r3.anchor: bunların delâletiyle hedefinizi, cihetlerinizi, kıblenizi, maddî mânevî yolunuzu doğrultasınız

ELMALILI:6:97/r4.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:6:97/r4.speaker: author
ELMALILI:6:97/r4.claim: Although the signs guide everyone and are stated concisely in many distinct points, their intellectual lessons especially benefit people capable of knowledge.

ELMALILI:6:97/r5.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:6:97/r5.speaker: author
ELMALILI:6:97/r5.claim: The created book is richly detailed across land, sea, earth, heaven, plants, animals, atmosphere, and celestial phenomena, and those capable of science can benefit from it.
ELMALILI:6:97/r5.anchor: kitab-ı hilkatte, berr ü bahrda, arz u semâda, nebâtât ve hayvânâtta, cevviyyât ve felekiyyâtta o kadar çok tafsîlâtı vardır

ELMALILI:6:97/r6.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:6:97/r6.speaker: author
ELMALILI:6:97/r6.claim: Elmalılı urges Muslims to study botany, zoology, calculation, observation, meteorological phenomena, and mathematical astronomy on these principles.
ELMALILI:6:97/r6.anchor: Müslümanlar bu düsturları esas ittihaz ederek nebâtât, hayvânât, hesab, rasad, âsâr-ı cevviye, hey’et-i riyâziye ilimlerini tahsîle

ELMALILI:6:97/r7.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:6:97/r7.speaker: author
ELMALILI:6:97/r7.claim: He invokes 18:109 to convey that the detailed sciences contained in these signs could not be exhausted even by the sea serving as ink.
ELMALILI:6:97/r7.anchor: قُل لَّوْ كَانَ ٱلْبَحْرُ مِدَادًۭا لِّكَلِمَٰتِ رَبِّى

ELMALILI:6:98-99#3/r5.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:6:98-99#3/r5.speaker: author
ELMALILI:6:98-99#3/r5.claim: The move from the audience who know to those who understand narrows the audience: analyzing these details requires more than ordinary learning, namely insight into the self.
ELMALILI:6:98-99#3/r5.anchor: evvelkinde لِقَوْمٍ يَعْلَمُونَ ile iktifâ olunduğu hâlde burada لِقَوْمٍۢ يَفْقَهُونَ buyurularak daha ziyade tahsis kılınmıştır.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:6:97/r1.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:6:97/r1.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:6:97/r1.claim: Travelers have long used stars and constellations to find direction, especially before the compass; this remains useful where modern facilities are unavailable.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:6:97/r1.anchor: İnsanlar çok eski dönemlerden beri yolculuk ederken yön tayininde bazı yıldızların ve yıldız kümelerinin konumundan yararlanırlar.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:6:97/r2.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:6:97/r2.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:6:97/r2.claim: Whether or not people navigate by them, the stars’ cosmic order remains a sign of divine power as long as God sustains it.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:6:97/r2.anchor: Yıldızların konumlarından yararlanılsın veya yararlanılmasın, onların kozmik düzeni –Allah bu düzeni devam ettirdiği sürece– ilâhî kudretin işareti olma özelliğini koruyacaktır.

BURHAN:v1p81/r4.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p81/r4.speaker: author
BURHAN:v1p81/r4.claim: Zarkashī points to the Anʿām passage about stars as a parallel set of three verse endings whose wording varies to fit each passage.
BURHAN:v1p81/r4.anchor: ونظير هذه الثلاث فواصل مع اختلافها قوله تعالى فى سورة الأنعام

ITQAN:v3p272/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p272/r4.speaker: author
ITQAN:v3p272/r4.claim: The statement about stars ends with “for people who know” because calculating by and navigating with the stars is the work of those skilled in that knowledge.
ITQAN:v3p272/r4.anchor: وذلك لأن حساب النجوم والاهتداء بها يختص بالعلماء
